blocks.text: Material configuration for primitives and models
texture: CDN path to texture; a video's address plays on the surface, a screen in the world: an .mp4 clip loops from its start, an .m3u8 address plays its live stream. The picture is silent:…

StandardMaterialSpec = { texture?: string | null // "cdn/x.png"; null: no picture (three's map = null). A model part reads "#<name>": the picture its model draws there. time?: number // The .mp4 clip's playhead in seconds: every player's screen shows `paused ? time : time + speed * (ctx.now() - timeAt) / 1000`, and a write jumps every screen. One address is one clip: the newest write on any surface wearing it moves it. An .m3u8 plays its live point. timeAt?: number // World-clock milliseconds (ctx.now()) at which `time` applies; the engine stamps it for you. paused?: boolean // true freezes the .mp4 clip on every player's screen on the frame it shows; false resumes it from the frame it holds. speed?: number // The .mp4 clip's playback speed on every player's screen (default 1; 0.5 is half speed): a write keeps the frame it shows and plays on at the new speed. view?: { link: string; oneWay?: boolean; spill?: number; sound?: number } | { camera: ViewCamera; cadence?: string; size?: number } | null // A view: the surface shows a place, drawn live. It fills the whole face exactly once (a viewport, never tiled); `texture` is ignored when `view` is set. `view: { link: "world:<id>" }` is a door's glass: the linked world or place seen through the face. Until that world's feed delivers it is a dim panel tinted with the world's own identity hue (deterministic, never an error). Both faces of an upright glass are windows, each showing the far world from its own side's landing; `oneWay: true` makes a one-sided door: the back face is a veiled wall and the door's trigger refuses a traveler on that side. A glass lying flat is a hole: looking down through it, you see the far place from one body length above the linked thing, looking where you look; looking up, the sky over it. So link a floor glass to a thing on the ground of what the floor should show. `spill` is how much of the far world's light comes through the aperture onto this world's ground and walls (0 none, 1 what a hole in a wall lets through: the default, 2 twice that); `sound` how much of the far world's sound is heard through it (0 a silent door, 1 physical: the default). A link to another world with no `@ref` shows it at the viewer's own copy: its build while they build, its live game while they play. `@live` in the link always shows the live game, `@dev` always the build. `view: { camera }` shows this place from a camera, or with `camera.place` another place of this world (`spawn api ViewCamera`): `camera: "mirror"` is a mirror, `camera: { eye, aim, fov }` a camera you place (a security monitor, a map), `camera: { parent: id }` one that rides a thing. The face's own `color` shows until its picture draws. `cadence: "1s"` draws one new picture a second, and `size: 256` draws it 256 pixels on its longer side; the engine serves both within the frame, and with neither it fits them to the face on the screen. canvas?: string | null // The id of a `<canvas>` in the game's ui: the surface shows it live, as the ui's script draws it (three's CanvasTexture). It fills the shape's own 0..1 UVs once, so a scripted screen returns `{ uvs }` 0..1; `repeat` and `wrap: "repeat"` tile it. It wins over `texture`, and a `view` wins over it. `material.canvas = "crt"` wears `<canvas id="crt">`; each player sees the canvas their own page drew. A name no canvas answers leaves the face its own colour, and null takes the canvas off. A canvas uploads every frame while a face wearing it is in view, so draw it at the size the glass needs. pbr?: boolean | "fal1" // true derives normal/roughness/metalness from the texture; omitted or false derives nothing, and a false you write reads back as false (ground materials differ: a heightmap albedo wears PBR unless pbr: false) normalMap?: string // three's map names at three's channels, linear data: a normal map; a roughness map (.g × roughness: unset roughness beside it lets the map own the surface); a metalness map (.b × metalness: unset metalness beside it reads as metal); an alpha map (.g × the texture's alpha: coverage under transparent, the cut under alphaTest). pbr: true derives the first three from the texture. three's other maps (displacementMap, aoMap, bumpMap) go on a scripted material's node material, as in three: m.displacementMap = ctx.texture(cdn) roughnessMap?: string metalnessMap?: string alphaMap?: string normalScale?: number // three's normalScale on a primitive: the normal map's relief × this (default 1; 0 flat; negative inverts it) alphaTest?: number // three's alphaTest: the alpha cutoff (0..1) under which a texel is cut color?: Color // beside a texture: recolours it, keeping its light and dark, by the colour's saturation (white = no-op, grey darkens); three's texel × colour: multiply in its texture script repeat?: [number, number] // [u,v] copies across the face; under wrap repeat, × the 1-tile-per-meter density textureScale?: number // meters per tile under wrap: "repeat" (divides the 1-tile-per-meter density; default 1); without wrap: "repeat" it reads nothing wrap?: "repeat" | "clamp" // omitted: the picture once across the surface: once around a sphere (a planet's equirectangular map), once per face of a box; repeat then counts copies. "repeat": the one word that tiles it, one tile per meter (fabric, brick, felt); the texture's name never decides filter?: "pixel" | "linear" // How the pictures this material names are sampled, as sprite.filter: "pixel" is three's NearestFilter up close (crisp pixel art, every texel a hard square), "linear" smooth. Unset: each picture's own default metalness?: number roughness?: number opacity?: number transparent?: boolean emissive?: Color // a Color; emissiveIntensity scales it emissiveIntensity?: number emissiveMap?: string // three's emissiveMap: a picture (sRGB) whose texels × emissive × emissiveIntensity light the surface; emissive must be set (black, the default, lights nothing) unlit?: boolean // true skips lighting: the color/texture and emissive land flat, no shade or shadow on the surface (three's MeshBasicMaterial); default false dissolve?: number // 0 intact → 1 gone; tween it for a spawn-in / death-out side?: "front" | "back" | "double" // three's side. A primitive draws every face unless set: "front" draws only the faces toward the viewer (a room's lining seen from inside and invisible from outside: it still casts its shadow), "back" only the faces away, "double" both. A model part: "double" for thin geometry seen from both sides vertexColors?: boolean // three's vertexColors. A model part: true (the default where its mesh has vertex colours, as three's GLTFLoader sets it) multiplies them into the colour; false draws the part as color × texture, so shading baked into the vertices is gone, not lightened. Models only: a primitive does not read it, so a custom primitive's colors still draw depthWrite?: boolean depthTest?: boolean renderOrder?: number // draw order among transparent things (higher draws later); in a 2D place it is a mesh's layer among sprite sortingLayers; a part that must read through another part of its own character wears drawsOver instead drawsOver?: string[] | { parts: string[]; strength?: number; angle?: number } // a model part: the names of parts of the same character this part shows through when they cover it (a character's eyes through that character's own hair): a see-through copy blended at strength (0..1, default 0.5) while the camera is within angle degrees of the part's facing (0..180, default 60); a bare array takes both defaults. The copy shows only through the named parts where they are solid (not blended); a solid surface in front of them, a hand or another character, hides it; a see-through or blended surface in front does not hide it and the copy draws over it. Under a player's "jaggies: no" setting the copy is not drawn and the part draws as it would without the word outline?: boolean | { color?: Color; width?: number; warm?: number; lightness?: number } | null // an ink line around it: true = a 2-pixel line in a darker shade of its own colour, lit as it is lit; width = that many pixels (of a 1080p picture) up close, up to 63 pixels of the picture drawn; color = shown as given, up to 0.9 of white on each channel; with no color, lightness = the shade's share of its surface's lightness (0..1, default 0.58) and warm = how far the shade leans to a warm brown (0..1, default 0); every line thins with distance and fogs as the world does; drawn only around opaque solids polygonOffset?: boolean // three's polygon offset: true biases this surface's depth by polygonOffsetFactor × its depth slope + polygonOffsetUnits × the depth step, negative toward the eye: a decal quad lying on a floor or a wall wins the depth test at every distance and angle (-1, -1 is the usual pair). Primitives only; its shadow ignores it polygonOffsetFactor?: number polygonOffsetUnits?: number blending?: "none" | "normal" | "additive" | "subtractive" | "multiply" | "custom" // three's blending, on a transparent surface: "normal" (default), "additive", "subtractive", "multiply", "none", or "custom", three's CustomBlending, which reads blendSrc (default "src-alpha"), blendDst ("one-minus-src-alpha") and blendEquation ("add"); the Alpha three take the alpha channel's, unset the colour's. "min" and "max" read no factor blendSrc?: BlendFactor blendDst?: BlendFactor blendEquation?: BlendEquation blendSrcAlpha?: BlendFactor blendDstAlpha?: BlendFactor blendEquationAlpha?: BlendEquation premultipliedAlpha?: boolean // three's premultipliedAlpha: the colour leaves multiplied by its alpha and the blend reads it so colorWrite?: boolean // three's colorWrite: false draws depth and no colour, an invisible mask that hides what draws after it (the sea and every see-through thing; solids with a higher renderOrder): a boat's hull keeps the water out under a mask at its waterline. Costs one draw that writes depth alone clippingPlanes?: ClipPlane[] | null // three's clippingPlanes, up to 8: the surface is cut where normal · p + constant < 0 for any plane, or for every plane under clipIntersection; clipShadows: true cuts its shadow too. A new constant moves the cut with no rebuild: a cut-away roof follows the player. Costs one test a plane on each pixel the surface covers, and a cut solid loses the early depth test, so wear it only on the pieces a cut crosses clipIntersection?: boolean clipShadows?: boolean overrides?: MaterialOverridesSpec }

StandardMaterialSpec = {
  texture?: string | null   // "cdn/x.png"; null: no picture (three's map = null). A model part reads "#<name>": the picture its model draws there.
  time?: number   // The .mp4 clip's playhead in seconds: every player's screen shows `paused ? time : time + speed * (ctx.now() - timeAt) / 1000`, and a write jumps every screen. One address is one clip: the newest write on any surface wearing it moves it. An .m3u8 plays its live point.
  timeAt?: number   // World-clock milliseconds (ctx.now()) at which `time` applies; the engine stamps it for you.
  paused?: boolean   // true freezes the .mp4 clip on every player's screen on the frame it shows; false resumes it from the frame it holds.
  speed?: number   // The .mp4 clip's playback speed on every player's screen (default 1; 0.5 is half speed): a write keeps the frame it shows and plays on at the new speed.
  view?: { link: string; oneWay?: boolean; spill?: number; sound?: number } | { camera: ViewCamera; cadence?: string; size?: number } | null   // A view: the surface shows a place, drawn live. It fills the whole face exactly once (a viewport, never tiled); `texture` is ignored when `view` is set. `view: { link: "world:<id>" }` is a door's glass: the linked world or place seen through the face. Until that world's feed delivers it is a dim panel tinted with the world's own identity hue (deterministic, never an error). Both faces of an upright glass are windows, each showing the far world from its own side's landing; `oneWay: true` makes a one-sided door: the back face is a veiled wall and the door's trigger refuses a traveler on that side. A glass lying flat is a hole: looking down through it, you see the far place from one body length above the linked thing, looking where you look; looking up, the sky over it. So link a floor glass to a thing on the ground of what the floor should show. `spill` is how much of the far world's light comes through the aperture onto this world's ground and walls (0 none, 1 what a hole in a wall lets through: the default, 2 twice that); `sound` how much of the far world's sound is heard through it (0 a silent door, 1 physical: the default). A link to another world with no `@ref` shows it at the viewer's own copy: its build while they build, its live game while they play. `@live` in the link always shows the live game, `@dev` always the build. `view: { camera }` shows this place from a camera, or with `camera.place` another place of this world (`spawn api ViewCamera`): `camera: "mirror"` is a mirror, `camera: { eye, aim, fov }` a camera you place (a security monitor, a map), `camera: { parent: id }` one that rides a thing. The face's own `color` shows until its picture draws. `cadence: "1s"` draws one new picture a second, and `size: 256` draws it 256 pixels on its longer side; the engine serves both within the frame, and with neither it fits them to the face on the screen.
  canvas?: string | null   // The id of a `<canvas>` in the game's ui: the surface shows it live, as the ui's script draws it (three's CanvasTexture). It fills the shape's own 0..1 UVs once, so a scripted screen returns `{ uvs }` 0..1; `repeat` and `wrap: "repeat"` tile it. It wins over `texture`, and a `view` wins over it. `material.canvas = "crt"` wears `<canvas id="crt">`; each player sees the canvas their own page drew. A name no canvas answers leaves the face its own colour, and null takes the canvas off. A canvas uploads every frame while a face wearing it is in view, so draw it at the size the glass needs.
  pbr?: boolean | "fal1"   // true derives normal/roughness/metalness from the texture; omitted or false derives nothing, and a false you write reads back as false (ground materials differ: a heightmap albedo wears PBR unless pbr: false)
  normalMap?: string   // three's map names at three's channels, linear data: a normal map; a roughness map (.g × roughness: unset roughness beside it lets the map own the surface); a metalness map (.b × metalness: unset metalness beside it reads as metal); an alpha map (.g × the texture's alpha: coverage under transparent, the cut under alphaTest). pbr: true derives the first three from the texture. three's other maps (displacementMap, aoMap, bumpMap) go on a scripted material's node material, as in three: m.displacementMap = ctx.texture(cdn)
  roughnessMap?: string
  metalnessMap?: string
  alphaMap?: string
  normalScale?: number   // three's normalScale on a primitive: the normal map's relief × this (default 1; 0 flat; negative inverts it)
  alphaTest?: number   // three's alphaTest: the alpha cutoff (0..1) under which a texel is cut
  color?: Color   // beside a texture: recolours it, keeping its light and dark, by the colour's saturation (white = no-op, grey darkens); three's texel × colour: multiply in its texture script
  repeat?: [number, number]   // [u,v] copies across the face; under wrap repeat, × the 1-tile-per-meter density
  textureScale?: number   // meters per tile under wrap: "repeat" (divides the 1-tile-per-meter density; default 1); without wrap: "repeat" it reads nothing
  wrap?: "repeat" | "clamp"   // omitted: the picture once across the surface: once around a sphere (a planet's equirectangular map), once per face of a box; repeat then counts copies. "repeat": the one word that tiles it, one tile per meter (fabric, brick, felt); the texture's name never decides
  filter?: "pixel" | "linear"   // How the pictures this material names are sampled, as sprite.filter: "pixel" is three's NearestFilter up close (crisp pixel art, every texel a hard square), "linear" smooth. Unset: each picture's own default
  metalness?: number
  roughness?: number
  opacity?: number
  transparent?: boolean
  emissive?: Color   // a Color; emissiveIntensity scales it
  emissiveIntensity?: number
  emissiveMap?: string   // three's emissiveMap: a picture (sRGB) whose texels × emissive × emissiveIntensity light the surface; emissive must be set (black, the default, lights nothing)
  unlit?: boolean   // true skips lighting: the color/texture and emissive land flat, no shade or shadow on the surface (three's MeshBasicMaterial); default false
  dissolve?: number   // 0 intact → 1 gone; tween it for a spawn-in / death-out
  side?: "front" | "back" | "double"   // three's side. A primitive draws every face unless set: "front" draws only the faces toward the viewer (a room's lining seen from inside and invisible from outside: it still casts its shadow), "back" only the faces away, "double" both. A model part: "double" for thin geometry seen from both sides
  vertexColors?: boolean   // three's vertexColors. A model part: true (the default where its mesh has vertex colours, as three's GLTFLoader sets it) multiplies them into the colour; false draws the part as color × texture, so shading baked into the vertices is gone, not lightened. Models only: a primitive does not read it, so a custom primitive's colors still draw
  depthWrite?: boolean
  depthTest?: boolean
  renderOrder?: number   // draw order among transparent things (higher draws later); in a 2D place it is a mesh's layer among sprite sortingLayers; a part that must read through another part of its own character wears drawsOver instead
  drawsOver?: string[] | { parts: string[]; strength?: number; angle?: number }   // a model part: the names of parts of the same character this part shows through when they cover it (a character's eyes through that character's own hair): a see-through copy blended at strength (0..1, default 0.5) while the camera is within angle degrees of the part's facing (0..180, default 60); a bare array takes both defaults. The copy shows only through the named parts where they are solid (not blended); a solid surface in front of them, a hand or another character, hides it; a see-through or blended surface in front does not hide it and the copy draws over it. Under a player's "jaggies: no" setting the copy is not drawn and the part draws as it would without the word
  outline?: boolean | { color?: Color; width?: number; warm?: number; lightness?: number } | null   // an ink line around it: true = a 2-pixel line in a darker shade of its own colour, lit as it is lit; width = that many pixels (of a 1080p picture) up close, up to 63 pixels of the picture drawn; color = shown as given, up to 0.9 of white on each channel; with no color, lightness = the shade's share of its surface's lightness (0..1, default 0.58) and warm = how far the shade leans to a warm brown (0..1, default 0); every line thins with distance and fogs as the world does; drawn only around opaque solids
  polygonOffset?: boolean   // three's polygon offset: true biases this surface's depth by polygonOffsetFactor × its depth slope + polygonOffsetUnits × the depth step, negative toward the eye: a decal quad lying on a floor or a wall wins the depth test at every distance and angle (-1, -1 is the usual pair). Primitives only; its shadow ignores it
  polygonOffsetFactor?: number
  polygonOffsetUnits?: number
  blending?: "none" | "normal" | "additive" | "subtractive" | "multiply" | "custom"   // three's blending, on a transparent surface: "normal" (default), "additive", "subtractive", "multiply", "none", or "custom", three's CustomBlending, which reads blendSrc (default "src-alpha"), blendDst ("one-minus-src-alpha") and blendEquation ("add"); the Alpha three take the alpha channel's, unset the colour's. "min" and "max" read no factor
  blendSrc?: BlendFactor
  blendDst?: BlendFactor
  blendEquation?: BlendEquation
  blendSrcAlpha?: BlendFactor
  blendDstAlpha?: BlendFactor
  blendEquationAlpha?: BlendEquation
  premultipliedAlpha?: boolean   // three's premultipliedAlpha: the colour leaves multiplied by its alpha and the blend reads it so
  colorWrite?: boolean   // three's colorWrite: false draws depth and no colour, an invisible mask that hides what draws after it (the sea and every see-through thing; solids with a higher renderOrder): a boat's hull keeps the water out under a mask at its waterline. Costs one draw that writes depth alone
  clippingPlanes?: ClipPlane[] | null   // three's clippingPlanes, up to 8: the surface is cut where normal · p + constant < 0 for any plane, or for every plane under clipIntersection; clipShadows: true cuts its shadow too. A new constant moves the cut with no rebuild: a cut-away roof follows the player. Costs one test a plane on each pixel the surface covers, and a cut solid loses the early depth test, so wear it only on the pieces a cut crosses
  clipIntersection?: boolean
  clipShadows?: boolean
  overrides?: MaterialOverridesSpec
}
